keep.brief: Spy (Allied, T2, barracks plus Radar Dome): cover the disguise that is always on (every viewer sees one of their own riflemen), each building's infiltration result as capture-structure sabotage (including the radar dome's shared vision and the one-shot sonar pulse and parabomb strike it grants), that it has no weapon, and the attack dog as its counter; note the Soviet Spy is campaign only.
keep.why: The batch's only infantry disguise and its capture-structure unit, a registry id with Red Alert examples. The disguise fools every viewer at once, and the payoff depends on the building. It pairs with the kept attack dog, its hard counter. The Spy line is kept once, here.

keep.brief: Attack Dog (Soviet, T1, Kennel): cover the bite that kills any soldier outright but cannot hurt vehicles or the ground, the rule of one dog per victim, its spy detection (sensor trait detector), its very low price and health, and propose execute-target.
keep.why: The very-low price band, the batch's only animal, and the clearest hard counter in the list: it exists to catch the Spy. Its one-bite kill is a mechanic no registry id covers.

keep.brief: Field Mechanic (Allied, The Aftermath, T2, Service Depot): cover its repair tool on friendly vehicles (repair-allies) and how it compares with the depot, that it has no weapon, the rule that it must repair a transport before it can board it, and introduced_in ra1-aftermath.
keep.why: The batch's only pure repairer and its only repair-allies unit. In a game where most players are vehicles, a repairer on foot is a core team role; the IFV sample only borrows a repair tool as a passenger weapon.

keep.brief: M.A.D. Tank (Soviet, The Aftermath, T3): cover the deploy that starts a long wind-up only its death can stop, the crewman who bails out and runs, the seismic pulse that takes a share of maximum health from every vehicle, ship, aircraft and building nearby, friend or foe, while sparing infantry (self-destruct; propose deal-percent-damage), and that the Iron Curtain blocks it.
keep.why: The richest self-destruct in the list: a telegraphed wind-up the enemy must answer, a crew that escapes, and damage by share of health that spares infantry, so infantry become its counter. It replaces the plainer RA2 Demolition Truck.

keep.brief: Mobile Gap Generator (Allied, T3, multiplayer only): cover the shroud it keeps wrapping around itself, how an enemy passing through lifts it near himself and it closes behind him, what it does for escorted units, that it has no weapon, that the AI ignores shroud, the multiplayer-only mark, the support-role fit (likely a role gap, with a fit_note), and propose shroud-area.
keep.why: The batch's odd one: it fights with information, not damage. Under Shamble's fog of war (decision 6C), hiding a whole group is real team play, and no registry id fits it (cloak, lay-smoke and jam-sensors each miss a part).

keep.brief: Minelayer (shared, T2, Service Depot): cover lay-mines with its stock of five refilled free at the depot, the mine chosen by the owner's side (anti-tank for the Allies, anti-personnel for the Soviets, which Soviet troops avoid), that it has no gun, the Yak sweeping its minefields, and settle one shared entry against one entry per side.
keep.why: The registry's own lay-mines example and the batch's area-denial primary. One chassis whose payload depends on the side is a neat faction twist for the generator.

keep.brief: Mammoth Tank (Soviet, T3, Tech Center): cover its two weapons and their mounts (twin cannons against armour, missile racks against infantry, buildings and aircraft), the self-repair that stops at half health, its armour class (RA1's map puts every tank in heavy), whether the crew-survivor rule applies when it dies, and its roles under the round-2 roles rules; opening-check unit.
keep.why: The batch's super-heavy assault tank, kept once for the Mammoth-to-Apocalypse line. It has two weapons split by target, anti-air on a tank and a capped self-repair. It is a heavy tank like the Overlord that split round 2's roles.

keep.brief: Yak (Soviet, T2, Airfield behind the Radar Dome): cover the high-air attack plane, its twin machine guns on strafing runs against infantry, its finite ammo and the trip home to rearm (longer for more rounds), forward-only handling, and force-firing the ground to clear minefields.
keep.why: The batch's only fixed-wing jet, a class Shamble wants (decision 6C). It adds forward-only handling and rearming at a pad, and it counters the kept Minelayer.

keep.brief: Submarine (Soviet, T1, Submarine Pen; naval, research only): cover burrow (hidden while submerged, exposed when it surfaces to fire torpedoes), that it cannot hit land or air, and its counters: the Destroyer's detection and depth charges and the sonar pulse a Spy earns.
keep.why: The batch's one ship, kept for the classic hide-and-surface burrow, which carries over to a burrowing land unit. It pairs with the kept Spy through the sonar pulse.

keep.brief: Chrono Legionnaire (Allied, T3, Battle Lab): cover movement that is only teleporting, with a frozen, exposed arrival that lasts longer the farther it jumps (mobility trait and teleport), the beam that holds a target out of time until it is erased, all or nothing (lock-in-stasis), using it to shield a friend, and its crush immunity.
keep.why: The registry's lock-in-stasis example and the batch's teleport unit. Both twists are distinct: every move is a jump, and its beam protects the target until it erases it.

keep.brief: Robot Tank (Allied, Yuri's Revenge, T2, Robot Control Center): cover the uncrewed hover tank (crew model remote), its shutdown when the Control Center falls or loses power (sinking if over water), its mind-control immunity and lack of veterancy, and propose depend-on-relay.
keep.why: A unit that hangs on a team building the enemy can kill, a mechanic no id covers. It is RA2's hover unit and the batch's iconic answer to the Mastermind.

keep.brief: Desolator (Iraq country unit, T2, Radar Tower): cover the rad cannon against infantry (no aircraft or buildings), and the deploy that floods an area with radiation (deploy-siege-mode plus leave-hazard-zone): it hurts both sides, stacks, reaches into water and forces submarines up, spares him, and fades slowly after he leaves.
keep.why: The registry's leave-hazard-zone example. The zone comes from a deploy, not a key, and it hurts his own team, which makes placement a team decision.

keep.brief: Boris (Soviet, Yuri's Revenge, T3, one at a time): cover his rifle that also hurts vehicles, the laser he holds on a building to call MiGs in from the map edge (two, four when elite), what breaks or aborts the strike and how lost jets are replaced (mark-target or bombard-area, settled by the pattern notes), his immunity to mind control and crushing from the manual's Gameplay Changes, and his availability.
keep.why: The batch's call-in: a held designator that both teams can play around, a very shooter-ready team mechanic. He is the only kept bombard-area or mark-target unit, and a second hero beside RA3's Tanya with a different kit.

keep.brief: Siege Chopper (Soviet, Yuri's Revenge, T3): cover both forms as modes (a low-air gunship whose machine gun hits infantry and aircraft but not armour, and a landed howitzer that outranges most defences), the land and lift ability (transform or deploy-siege-mode), the grounded weaknesses (no moving, misses fast targets, pack-up delay, open to mind control), its price after patch 1.001, and its death; opening-check unit.
keep.why: One unit that moves between low air and the ground, with a different weapon and different threats in each. It also carries the batch's long-range artillery once the V2 is cut.

keep.brief: Mastermind (Yuri, Yuri's Revenge, T3, Battle Lab): cover mind control of every valid enemy nearby with no cap and no off switch, the overload damage past three captives (propose overload-past-cap), the units immune to it, and that control is its only weapon.
keep.why: The registry's mind-control id, whose folded example is RA2's psychic control. The overload turns its strength into its weakness and hands the enemy a counter: rush it with cheap units.

keep.brief: Magnetron (Yuri, Yuri's Revenge, T2, Psychic Radar): cover the beam that lifts a vehicle, hauls it close and drops it (pull-target, lift variant), the lifted vehicle counting as an air target and dying if dropped into water or onto units, the same beam as slow artillery against buildings that anti-air can't stop, and its lack of any answer to infantry.
keep.why: The registry's pull-target example. It sets up kills for teammates or the map, a setup-and-finish team play, and replaces the RA3 Apocalypse's harpoon in this batch.

keep.brief: Chaos Drone (Yuri, Yuri's Revenge, T1, War Factory as the YR manual's tech table shows): cover the unarmed drone's gas that sends nearby enemies berserk for about ten seconds (confuse-enemies), why victims fire faster and go for their own side first while ignoring the drone, the immune units, and how it can backfire on its own troops.
keep.why: The first sourced example for confuse-enemies, which has none yet. It differs from the Mastermind: it takes no control and only turns enemies on each other.

keep.brief: Slave Miner (Yuri, Yuri's Revenge, T1, War Factory or Construction Yard; from the researcher's alternates): cover the vehicle that deploys into a refinery building, the up to five Slaves it releases to gather ore and replaces free when they die (gather-resources; check reinforce-squad), how to record the Slaves (separate units), its self-repair while mobile and engineer-only repair when deployed, its gun, its immunity to mind control and Terror Drones, the logistics role, and the patch 1.001 price.
keep.why: No listed candidate covers gather-resources, whose registry examples are RA2 miners, so this comes from the researcher's named logistics alternate (its wiki page and manual entry exist). It is the batch's only logistics unit and a vehicle that becomes a building.

keep.brief: Mecha Tengu (Empire, T1, Mecha Bay): cover both forms as modes (a hover skimmer that shreds infantry and light vehicles, a jet that can only shoot aircraft), each form's armour and counters, the switch cooldown, the crash when it dies as a jet, the hover class choice, and roles from its one designation for both forms.
keep.why: The cleanest transform (a brief pattern) and the batch's switch between the ground and high air, from the Empire, which no sample covers.

keep.brief: Sudden Transport (Empire, T1, Mecha Bay): cover carry-passengers (five seats, amphibious hover), the disguise that copies any vehicle it targets and drops when riders get out, who sees through it (dogs, war bears, Burst Drones, and its own speed), its blast on death, and roles step 1 from the manual paragraph, since it has no profile page.
keep.why: The batch's only transport and its carry-passengers unit, a brief pattern. Its disguise holds while it carries a squad, a twist the Spy lacks, and it adds a second Empire unit.

keep.brief: Sickle (Soviet, T1, War Factory): cover Flea Jump (leap) over walls and up cliffs, with damage and infantry crushing where it lands, and its cooldown; its three machine guns and their partly overlapping arcs (mounts); the walker class and legs; and what it can't hit or cross (aircraft, water).
keep.why: The batch's only walker. Its leap lands with a slam, and three guns with separate arcs test the mount rules.

keep.brief: Kirov Airship (Soviet, T3, Airfield plus Battle Lab): cover the high-air airship, its bombs that reach only what is below and still hurt friends at reduced strength, its lack of anti-air, the Gastroburners that about double its speed while burning its own hull (overclock-self), its toughness and slowness, and the crash on death.
keep.why: The batch's only airship, a class Shamble wants. The Kirov line is kept once, here, because RA3's speed boost paid in health is a clear twist over RA2's.

keep.brief: Tanya (Allied, T3, Boot Camp, one per player): cover the Time Belt that sends her back about five seconds in place and health (propose rewind-self), her twin pistols, C4 planted on vehicles, ships and buildings (throw-explosive, planted variant), swimming and fighting in water, unique availability, and the Defense Bureau gate from patch 1.11.
keep.why: The Tanya line is kept once, here: RA3 adds the Time Belt, a clear twist, and C4 on vehicles. She is the batch's commando and hero.

keep.brief: Cryocopter (Allied, T2, Airbase): cover the cryobeam that slows and then freezes surface targets so they shatter (freeze-and-shatter), the SHRINK beam (propose shrink-target), switching between the two beams, that it deals no real damage and never ranks up, and low air.
keep.why: Control without damage, and the shrink mechanic the pattern notes flagged as 'to check'. It is a low-air disabler, unlike any sample.

cut.reason: Repeat of the Tanya line. RA3's Tanya (kept) has the same twin pistols, planted C4 and one-per-player cap, and adds the Time Belt, a clear twist, so the line is kept once, there.

Teleport is carried by the RA2 Chrono Legionnaire (kept), whose jumps have their own twist (every move is a jump, with a frozen arrival). The tank's other lessons, twin anti-armour missiles on a glass cannon, are plain word-list terms.

Low air is covered by the Siege Chopper and the Cryocopter, and the Yak (kept) teaches the same finite ammo and rearming at a pad. The plain attack helicopter returns with Battlefield in batch R6 and was already coded in the pilot.

Links no pattern: its lessons (lobbed, friendly fire, escort dependency) are word-list terms. The Siege Chopper's landed howitzer carries long-range siege in this batch, and artillery returns in many later batches.

It would be RA2's third deploy unit: the Desolator and the Siege Chopper already teach deploy-siege-mode, and the Siege Chopper's deploy also swaps its weapon and threats, as the GI's does. Its crush immunity when deployed goes in the report as a word-list gap (Boris and the Chrono Legionnaire have it too). It is the first swap back if RA2 needs more Allied weight.

Repeat of the Spy line. Its building results (blackout, money and tech theft, radar reset, promotions) are more of the capture-structure sabotage the RA1 Spy (kept) teaches, so the later game adds no clear twist. The line stays once, as the RA1 Spy, which also pairs with the kept RA1 attack dog.

Repeat of the Kirov line. RA3's Kirov (kept) adds a clear twist, the speed boost paid in health, and keeps the slow bomber, bombs that drop only below, and the crash on death. The RA2 build warning (announce-arrival) is left out with it.

Self-destruct is carried by the RA1 M.A.D. Tank (kept), which adds more twists (wind-up, crew bail-out, damage by share of health that spares infantry), and a deadly wreck by the RA3 Kirov's crash. The truck's ram delivery and the Chrono Legionnaire's clean answer to it can go in the self-destruct pattern file as sourced examples.

Its building sabotage (switching off defences, blackout, money siphon) repeats the Spy's capture-structure results from outside, and its build warning is announce-arrival, left out with the RA2 Kirov. Yuri already has four picks with stronger lessons, and low air is covered by the Siege Chopper and the Cryocopter.

Repeat of the submarine lesson: the RA1 Submarine (kept) is the batch's ship and also hides underwater and surfaces to fire. Naval is research only, so one ship is enough; the missile that can be shot down goes in the report as a possible weapon trait.

Its Spider Burrow digs in place (no moving, no firing, less damage, crush-proof), closer to brace than to the hide-and-surface burrow the Submarine teaches. With six RA3 slots, the Empire picks go to the Mecha Tengu (transform) and the Sudden Transport (the only transport), and the RA1 dog covers the very-low band.

It continues the Mammoth line, which R1 keeps once, as the RA1 Mammoth (also an opening-check unit). Its harpoon is pull-target, which the Magnetron carries; the pull-target pattern file can cite the harpoon page as a second variant. RA3 already has two Soviet samples.

It overlaps the Multigunner IFV sample (a cheap T1 carrier whose gun hits only aircraft), and its catapult is close to drop-in-from-above, as its researcher says. The Sudden Transport carries carry-passengers for RA3 and adds an Empire unit instead of a fifth Soviet one.

Naval is research only and the RA1 Submarine is the batch's ship. draw-fire and brace stay for later batches (brace already has Dawn of War II examples from the pilot); its Black Hole Armor can be cited in a draw-fire pattern file as a sourced example.

opening_reason: They come from two games other than RA3, and neither game's notes were tested in the pilot: RA1 reads EA's released source code and the manual, RA2 the Yuri's Revenge manual and ModEnc. Between them they cover the contested fields. Roles: the Mammoth is a heavy tank like the round-2 Overlord, which split on assault against anti-armour, with anti-air missiles as a likely secondary (secondary roles was the only field under 80% in round 2); the Siege Chopper's role changes with its form. Seats and mounts: twin cannons and missile racks on one tank; a gunship's gun and a landed howitzer. Several weapons: two each, with targets split by weapon on the Mammoth and by mode on the Chopper. Abilities with patterns: land and lift reads as transform or deploy-siege-mode, and sets the modes count. Death: RA1's crew-survivor rule against the bail-out default, and a helicopter's death. They also test the armour class (RA1 maps every tank to heavy) and the self-repair armour model. Neither needs a new pattern, so a split points at word lists 1.0, not at a missing id.
coverage: KEPT: 24 units (RA1 9, RA2 9, RA3 6, plus the three RA3 samples). The Slave Miner comes from the RA2 researcher's named alternates, not the candidate list, because no candidate covers gather-resources. CLASSES: infantry 7 (Spy, Attack Dog, Field Mechanic, Chrono Legionnaire, Desolator, Boris, Tanya); vehicles 7 (M.A.D. Tank, Mobile Gap Generator, Minelayer, Mammoth, Mastermind, Magnetron, Slave Miner) plus two samples; walker 1 (Sickle, the only one in the three games); hover 3 (Robot Tank, Mecha Tengu, Sudden Transport); drone 1 (Chaos Drone) plus the Terror Drone sample; aircraft 4: low air Siege Chopper and Cryocopter, high air Yak (jet) and Kirov (airship), plus the Tengu's jet form; naval 1 (Submarine, research only). Odd ones: the war dog, the unarmed shroud truck, the teleport-only Legionnaire, the helicopter that lands as artillery, and the miner that becomes a building. FACTIONS: RA1 Allied 3, Soviet 5, shared 1; RA2 Allied 2, Soviet 3 (Desolator as Iraq), Yuri 4; RA3 Allied 2, Soviet 2, Empire 2 (with samples: Soviet 4, Allied 3, Empire 2). Allied is light in RA1 and RA2 because the cut Allied units were repeats (Tanya, Spy) or were taught by another kept unit (Chrono Tank, Longbow, Guardian GI); the Guardian GI is the first swap back if that matters more. TIERS: T1 7, T2 8, T3 9 (samples add T1 2, T2 1). PRICE BANDS: very low 1 (dog), low 6, medium 7, high 3, very high 7. ROLES (primary): anti-infantry, anti-armour, assault (Mammoth), siege (Siege Chopper, Kirov), infiltrator (Spy), support (Field Mechanic; Gap Generator by the wiki's label, a likely role gap), transport (Sudden Transport), logistics (Slave Miner), area-denial (Minelayer), disabler (Legionnaire, Mastermind, Magnetron, Chaos Drone, Cryocopter). Raider and anti-air appear as secondaries (anti-air primary is on the IFV sample). Not covered: buffer, engineer, and scout and marksman as primaries (only the samples' secondaries). REGISTRY IDS COVERED: disguise, capture-structure, repair-allies, self-destruct, lay-mines, burrow, teleport, lock-in-stasis, deploy-siege-mode, leave-hazard-zone, mark-target, bombard-area, transform, mind-control, pull-target, confuse-enemies (its first sourced example), gather-resources, carry-passengers, overclock-self, leap, throw-explosive, freeze-and-shatter, switch-weapon-mode, perhaps reinforce-squad (Slave Miner, to check); the samples add infest-vehicle, leech-weapon-on-kill, passenger-sets-weapon and disable-machine. Ids registered with Red Alert examples: capture-structure, pull-target, lock-in-stasis, gather-resources, lay-mines and leave-hazard-zone are all covered. earn-veterancy is game-wide, so it goes in each game's notes, not on a unit. launch-drones' RA example (the RA2 carrier) is the weapon family drone-launcher, per the correction, so it is left to later batches. Brief patterns: deploy-siege-mode, transform, disguise and carry-passengers are covered; raise-shield is not, because no candidate has a shield (the RA3 researcher's backup is the Athena Cannon). LEFT OUT: draw-fire and brace (Assault Destroyer), drop-in-from-above (Bullfrog), dash (King Oni backup), hijack-vehicle (Natasha backup), cloak and jam-sensors (RA1 Radar Jammer), become-invulnerable (the Iron Curtain is a support power). The ids proposed for cut units are dropped with them: announce-arrival (RA2 Kirov, Floating Disc), drain-structure (Floating Disc), launch-interceptable-missile (Boomer), launch-passengers (Bullfrog). share-enemy-vision (RA1 Spy) is not listed as new: like the RA2 Spy's money and tech theft, it is an infiltration result under capture-structure's sabotage variant. WORD-LIST GAPS TO CARRY to the report: crush immunity (Legionnaire, Boris, and the cut Guardian GI), and possibly one-hit kills and damage by share of health, if the merge pass makes execute-target and deal-percent-damage weapon traits rather than patterns.

new_patterns.summary: A close attack that kills one target of a set kind outright, whatever its health or armour, and does nothing to anything else. The merge pass may make it a weapon trait instead.

A hit or pulse that takes a fixed share of each target's maximum health instead of a set amount, so it hurts the heaviest unit as much as the lightest and a few hits kill anything. It may fit better as a weapon trait.

Wrap the ground around you in fog for the enemy, hiding you and nearby allies from enemies outside it. An enemy who comes close sees normally around himself, and the fog closes again behind him. Firing does not break it and detectors do not counter it, which sets it apart from cloak's area variant, lay-smoke and jam-sensors.
The unit works only while a linked team building or relay stands and has power. If it falls, every such unit shuts down where it is (one over water sinks) until it is rebuilt.
The unit keeps taking captives or stacks with no off switch. Past a safe number it takes growing damage until it sheds some. The merge pass may fold it into mind-control as a variant.
On a key, snap back to where you were a few seconds ago, with the health you had then, and then wait out a recharge.

Shrink an enemy vehicle for a time: it moves faster but reaches less far, hits weaker and takes more damage, and full-size vehicles can run it over. Soldiers are immune. The step-1 pattern notes held it back as 'to check'.
